baseline: Existing uncommitted workspace, file-panel, profile, workflow, and document changes are preserved.
initial_status: The supplied screenshot shows an SSH workspace workflow at run_shell call 32. Tool calls execute serially; a remote command can use the configured 60-second timeout, while heartbeat events only reset the watchdog without updating visible status.
acceptance: A workflow step cannot execute an unbounded number of tool calls; it stops with an actionable message at a documented per-step budget.
A running remote tool visibly reports that its connection is alive and its elapsed duration continues to update.
Cancelling a remote shell command terminates the local SSH client promptly and retains the existing per-command timeout behavior.
Focused server and JavaScript checks pass; browser acceptance is recorded separately when the local certificate blocks automation.
scope: Workflow tool-loop budget, remote SSH process lifecycle, run-status frontend, focused tests, task record, and necessary PRD/architecture notes.

requirements.summary: The screenshot and inspected run path identify a long, serial remote run_shell chain with non-visible heartbeat as the user-facing failure mode.

design.summary: Use a per-step budget because one model response can contain multiple serial calls; surface the existing 15-second heartbeat as visible connection activity; give the local SSH client a bounded post-cancel wait.

implementation.summary: Workflow steps now stop after 24 tool calls with an actionable message. SSH client waits are bounded after cancellation. The run panel displays connection-active after a heartbeat and updates the active tool duration every second.

verification.summary: Focused Docker Go regression exited 0, covering local cancellation, SSH workspace dispatch, and SSH cancellation. JavaScript syntax, localization integrity, and diff whitespace checks passed. Browser UI acceptance was not run because the local HTTPS certificate is not trusted by the automation browser.
